agency: South Dakota Department of Social Services (DSS), Division of Economic Assistance
admin_note: South Dakota is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program — DSS's Division of Economic Assistance administers directly through Economic Assistance Benefits Specialists (EABS), with no county-level policy authority, structurally similar to this roster's Nebraska, Connecticut, North Carolina, Ohio, New Jersey, Tennessee, Indiana, Missouri, Maryland, Colorado, South Carolina, Alabama, Louisiana, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Utah, Iowa, Arkansas, Mississippi, Kansas, New Mexico, and New Hampshire packs. FLAGSHIP STRUCTURAL FINDING: South Dakota is one of only a small handful of states (this pack found consistent secondary-source claims of six: SD, Kansas, Mississippi, North Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, and Wyoming — a seven-name list depending on the source, though this pack independently confirms only South Dakota's own status) that does NOT run Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) — South Dakota's own DSS SNAP Policy and Procedure Manual (updated July 2026, fetched directly and cleanly, HTTP 200) confirms a strict 130% FPG gross-income / 100% FPG net-income test for non-categorically-eligible households, with categorical eligibility reserved narrowly for actual TANF/Tribal TANF/SSI/Child Care Services recipients (Section 7700) — not a BBCE-style income-ceiling expansion. SECOND FLAGSHIP FINDING, a genuine correction of a stale, still widely-repeated secondary-source dollar figure: several current secondary sources (aggregator sites) quote South Dakota's SNAP resource limits as $2,750 (most households) / $4,250 (elderly/disabled) — this pack's direct fetch of DSS's own July-2026 manual, Section 9010, shows the CURRENT figures are $4,500 (elderly/disabled) / $3,000 (all other households), matching the current national FFY2026 cycle. THIRD FINDING, a genuine primary-source confirmation of a minority-position claim (South Dakota FULLY opted out of the federal drug-felony SNAP ban): DSS's own manual contains NO drug-felony-conviction disqualification provision anywhere — its only felon-disqualification section (7370, effective for convictions after 2/7/2014) covers solely the 2014 Farm Bill's violent/sex-offense list (aggravated sexual abuse, murder, child sexual exploitation, sexual assault), not drug convictions — and this pack cross-checked that silence against South Dakota Codified Law 28-12-3, which a secondary legal-research source (Collateral Consequences Resource Center) quotes directly as South Dakota's 2020 statutory opt-out under Pub. L. 104-193 § 115(d)(1)(A) of the § 115(a)(2) federal ban; see criminal-justice-disqualifications supplement. FOURTH FINDING: South Dakota's own manual explicitly names a Native American ABAWD work-requirement exemption (Section 13222, ACCESS code 'I') applying to any Native American individual living ANYWHERE in the state (not restricted to on-reservation residency), and separately documents FDPIR/SNAP mutual exclusivity rules (Sections 3902/5026) — see ABAWD and FDPIR notes below. FIFTH FINDING, an internal-document inconsistency this pack caught rather than silently resolved: DSS's own manual Table of Contents (page 9) lists the Standard Utility Allowance as $850/LUA $238/OUA $98/PUA $54, while the manual's OWN BODY TEXT (Sections 10400 and 10411, stated twice, consistently) gives SUA $950/LUA $265/OUA $109/PUA $60 — this pack treats the twice-repeated body-text figures as authoritative and flags the Table of Contents as a stale, unrevised summary page DSS did not update alongside the body text; see shelter-utility-deductions supplement.
system: DSS's Division of Economic Assistance processes SNAP centrally through Economic Assistance Benefits Specialists (EABS) — no county office has independent SNAP policy authority. Applicants apply online through the eaPortal (eaportal.sd.gov), by mail, or in person/by phone through a local DSS office; the eaPortal accepts either a full electronic application or just page one (name, address, signature) to start the process, with the rest completable later. South Dakota's Minnehaha and Pennington Counties (and the manual's Chapter Thirteen table of contents separately lists Yankton County) run Employment & Training (E&T) as MANDATORY for certain work registrants — a county-level program-operations distinction, though eligibility policy itself remains uniform statewide. This pack flags SD's manual as internally current (dated 'Updated July 2026' on its own cover page) and free of any WAF/bot-detection access barrier this pack encountered — dss.sd.gov served the manual PDF and consumer pages cleanly on the first direct curl attempt with a standard browser User-Agent.

verification.method: dss.sd.gov returned a clean HTTP 200 to every direct curl attempt this pack made, with a standard desktop browser User-Agent — NO WAF/bot-detection barrier of any kind, unlike several other states this roster has built. This pack's single access hiccup was navigational, not a genuine barrier: the state's short-form landing URL (dss.sd.gov/economicassistance/snap/) returned a 404, but the correct URL (dss.sd.gov/economicassistance/snap.aspx, found via WebSearch) and the direct manual PDF URL (dss.sd.gov/docs/economicassistance/snap/snapmanual.pdf, also found via WebSearch) both fetched cleanly on the first attempt. This pack extracted the manual's text with `pdftotext -layout` (17,261 lines) rather than a markdown-converting fetch tool, specifically to preserve the manual's numbered-section structure and multi-column example tables without mangling, and cross-checked every dollar figure against at least the manual's own repeated occurrences (the SUA figures appear identically in two separate body sections) plus, where available, a second independent source (South Dakota Codified Law 28-12-3's text via a secondary legal-research quote, and USDA's own ABAWD waiver index).
